authority: Ministry of AYUSH / Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO)
title: Definition of Classical Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani (ASU) Drug
content:
Section 3(a) defines an 'Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug' as including all medicines intended for internal or external use for or in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or prevention of disease or disorder in human beings or animals, and manufactured exclusively in accordance with the formulae described in the authoritative books of Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Tibb systems of medicine, specified in the First Schedule.

Key Consequences:
1. Authoritative Texts: Must be cited in the 54 recognized classical Ayurvedic texts (e.g., Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Astanga Hridaya, Sahasrayoga, Bhaishajya Ratnavali, Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India).
2. IP Posture: Zero patentability under Section 3(p) of Patents Act (prior art).
3. Regulatory Burden: Exempt from new drug clinical trials; requires classical manufacturing license from State Licensing Authority (AYUSH).
